description.narrative: Having been signed in early 2022, the CPD is going into its mid-year of implementation and is fairly on track. The portfolio has grown resulting in a large and diverse portfolio of projects across a range of sectors, and now with a field presence and a healthy pipeline. The CO’s resource envelope and delivery has grown exponentially, from US$19.6 million to US$34 million in the past three years. In 2024-25, the CO will seek to venture into new areas, testing innovations with scaling-up potential for achieving upstream policy results, evaluation, assessments, and crisis response, based on priorities to promote resilience, identified in the ENDE, PQG, UNSDCF, UNDP Strategic Plan and CPD. It will focus on areas deemed high value investments with potential for a return, including financing resilience in Mozambique, including tapping into climate finance, energy transition, etc.The CO will also seek establish a new workstream on inclusive growth/livelihoods to bring into coherence and structure the CO’s investments in inclusive growth/economic transformation at the national and sub-national level, specially creating synergies with the livelihoods and economic recovery offered under existing projects, especially the MRF and stabilization, and support an ecosystem approach to entrepreneurship/job creation. To ensure rapid response and the flexibility to do so, management will reserve up to 5 per cent of its annual Trac1 allocation in a ‘Rapid Response Facility (RRF)’, enabling it to explore and invest in these new areas.

condition.narrative: The Implementing Partner shall ensure that all of its obligations set forth under the section entitled “Legal Context and/or Risk Management Standard Clauses” are passed on to each responsible party, subcontractor and sub-recipient and that all the clauses under this section entitled “Risk Management” are included, mutatis mutandis, in all sub-contracts or sub-agreements entered into further to the Project Document
